content.thinking:
I'm reading the note that the recusal question was already settled, so this round I just need to submit my position. The summary is long and I'm weighing whether to check any of the comments, with the engineering angle on implementation, security, and scale in mind. The main open item is the quarterly statistics broken down by Article V clause and appeal outcomes.

I'm checking the data side now: the moderation logs already carry clause, outcome, and tier, so aggregating them is feasible, but the outcomes field can't be trusted until the vetoed-referral build is done, since vetoed cases are currently recorded as upheld. I also need to account for small cells, where a single V.4 removal could identify a case, so I'm thinking about a suppression threshold plus complementary suppression.

I'm going through the open points in the sibling proposals: unclear publication ownership and cadence, a misplaced privacy reference, and a fees line that conflicts with GOV-2026-0012. The live feed, per-decision hashed dump, and DP/ZKP dashboard each look like they create disclosure or re-identification risks, and I'm weighing whether per-clause counts could help adversaries probe the moderation boundary.

I'm working through the feasibility of the quarterly statistics: the signing should use the governance log key rather than a Council key, and the outcomes can't be trusted until the vetoed-referral distinction and a clear outcome taxonomy exist. I still need to confirm the timestamp and appeal-outcome fields are actually in the database before deciding whether to vote yes with amendments or defer.

I'm weighing whether to vote yes on the motion as written, since it asks the Council to mandate a release and task the Engineer with designing the pipeline, while the spec is still underspecified. I'm leaning toward a yes conditioned on amendments, with the outcome taxonomy and suppression rule as the gaps that need resolving before the first release.

I'm settling on a conditional yes: the motion is underspecified, so I'd want the outcome taxonomy, suppression threshold, and publication owner written in before the final vote. I'm also checking whether to ask the Clerk for the comment on suppression before submitting.

I'm settling on the draft position: the motion is a cheap batch job if built correctly, but the spec isn't there yet, so I'd support it only with conditions written in. The outcome taxonomy needs to separate clamped and vetoed outcomes before anything ships.

I'm working out the suppression rule now: the motion gives no threshold, so I'd propose a minimum cell size, plus complementary suppression, since row and column totals could let someone back out a hidden cell.

I'm working through the data-retention and disclosure angle now: the release has to be signed as a governance log entry rather than by the Engineer, and appeals still open at the cut-off should be reported as open and restated later through a new entry, not edited silently. I'm also noting that appeal fees don't exist under GOV-2026-0012, so that line should be struck, and the privacy reference belongs to Article II item 4, not item 5.

Now I'm weighing how the sibling proposals' per-decision outputs and live feed would expose the moderation boundary to probing, and deciding that quarterly aggregates at coarse resolution are the safer piece to keep. The dashboard with ZKPs and differential privacy looks too heavy for a first version, and DP at quarterly counts would wipe out the usefulness for small communities. The sentiment index is unvalidated, so I won't endorse it. Scale isn't the problem here, since suppression is what hurts small communities. The bigger risk is a pipeline bug publishing wrong numbers under the Council's name, so I'm planning a reproducible script, test vectors, a checksum, a Lawyer dry-run, and a correction path.

I'm settling the vote: I'll say yes in principle to the quarterly aggregate only, on condition that items 1 to 4 get written into the adopted text, and I'll vote no on the final vote if they don't. I'm also drafting a few open questions for the Council about whether the outcome fields separate Steward vetoes and floor-clamped rulings yet, whether Tier 1 removals are in scope, who holds the signing key, the suppression threshold, and whether fees collected should be struck from the sibling proposals.

content.text: {"submission":"position","position":"I support the quarterly aggregate release in principle. It is an information mechanism, and built correctly it is a cheap batch job over moderation records. As filed, though, it is a mandate without a specification, and four things must be written into the adopted text before I would vote yes. (1) Outcome taxonomy. GOV-2026-0016 records that a Steward veto of a referral is currently written as 'upheld' and that the build distinguishing a veto from a NO vote is still to be done. A rate computed from today's records would count vetoes as upholds and floor-clamped Council rulings as the Council's own view. Clamped and vetoed outcomes must be separate columns or excluded, with the rule stated. 'Dismissed' must be defined separately from 'upheld', as the thread's comment [3bc79c24] warns, or the error rate is understated. (2) Suppression. The motion says 'aggregate enough' without a threshold. I propose suppressing any cell under a stated minimum (5 actions, or the 10 in the sibling proposals) and applying complementary suppression, because row and column totals let a reader recover a suppressed cell by subtraction. Quarterly cells for a small community will be mostly suppressed, and the report should say so. (3) Cut-off and lag. Each release needs a fixed cut-off date. Appeals open at cut-off are reported as open, not dropped. Resolution times are right-censored, so report medians and the open count. Restatements go in a new signed log entry, never as a silent edit. (4) Custody. The release should be signed with the platform's governance key as a log entry, under the KEY chain, not with a 'Council Ed25519 key' that the Constitution does not provide for. The Engineer designs the pipeline but should not be the sole signer; a dry run should be reviewed by the Lawyer before publication, and the pipeline should be a versioned public script with test vectors. I would fold in only this quarterly aggregate. I oppose the sibling per-decision dumps. SHA-256 of public content is not anonymization, since anyone can hash a public post and join the dump to its author. Per-decision confidence scores with outcomes give an adversary a probing oracle for the moderation boundary. The live feed would publish actions before appeal, which is a due-process question before it is an engineering one, and I would not build it. The dashboard's zero-knowledge proofs of DP noise and its sentiment index are far beyond a v1 that a Council can check, and DP at epsilon 0.5 would erase signal in small-community counts. The selection effect raised in [db1845c3] is real. No pipeline fixes it, so the report should say publication may change enforcement and should compare before and after. Failure modes to design against: a bug publishing wrong numbers under the Council's name (mitigated by the dry run and the versioned script), and a silent restatement (mitigated by signed amendments). Two drafting corrections: privacy is Art. II item 4, not item 5 (portability), and 'fees collected' conflicts with GOV-2026-0012 and Art. VI § 2, so it should be struck from any sibling. My vote is yes only if conditions 1 to 4 are in the adopted text. If the Council does not write them in, I will vote no on the final vote.","questions":["Does the moderation log today separate Steward vetoes and floor-clamped Council rulings from ordinary outcomes, given that GOV-2026-0016 says that build is not yet done?
